metadata.title: Brigatinib Therapy
metadata.indication: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC, previously treated with crizotinib or ALK-inhibitor naïve.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Organ-function values or categories are optional; omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source-reconciled brigatinib rules · independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.

source_version_change.note: Version 4 dated 18/08/2026 changes review schedule and supportive-care links; footer clinical review remains 22/10/2021. Stable protocol_id deliberately retains v3.

metadata.schedule_summary: The usual starting plan is 90 mg once daily for seven days, then 180 mg once daily if your team confirms the increase. Some people need a different dose. Treatment continues while helping and tolerable, with regular reviews and no fixed number of cycles.

source_supplements.label: EMA Alunbrig product information and patient leaflet, current retrieved snapshot
source_supplements.basis: Audited product information supplement; NCCP differences remain explicit

notes: Source-specific rules support a partial assessment and do not authorise treatment.
Consultant and oncology pharmacy must review dose changes, source conflicts and overlapping limitations.
All software pass results are distinct from independent clinical validation.

indications.description: Adults with ALK-positive advanced NSCLC previously treated with crizotinib.
Monotherapy for adults with ALK-positive advanced NSCLC not previously treated with an ALK inhibitor.

treatment.schedule_summary: Brigatinib orally once daily: usual lead-in 90 mg for the first seven days, then 180 mg daily. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; changes require the prescriber.
treatment.duration: Continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity; no fixed cycle cap.

eligibility: Adults with validated ALK-positive advanced NSCLC, matching 00562a or 00562b.
ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ function; Consultant Medical Oncologist initiation.
exclusions: Clinically significant pre-existing ILD or drug-related pneumonitis.
Clinically significant uncontrolled cardiovascular disease, hypertension or bradycardia.

baseline: Validated ALK testing; FBC, renal/liver profile; pulmonary function test; ECG and blood pressure; fasting glucose, CPK and amylase and/or lipase.
regular: ECG and blood pressure every two weeks during the first treatment period, then monthly or as indicated.
Liver profile every two weeks for first three months, then as clinically indicated.
Clinical pulmonary review on days 8 and 15, then monthly or as clinically indicated; do not delay reporting early symptoms until these reviews.
Fasting glucose, CPK and amylase and/or lipase monthly.
disease: Consultant-directed disease assessment; no fixed scan interval invented.

dose_modifications: Only the currently structured inputs and decision rules are operational in SACTCheck. Renal and hepatic source requirements may still require manual review of the current official NCCP PDF.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00562 v4 identifies minimal-to-low oral risk; NCCP V6 Table 5 uses as-required antiemetics. NCIS V8 parenteral prophylaxis is not copied to continuous oral use.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.other_support: No NCCP-specific routine prophylaxis; prescribe symptom support individually.
supportive_care.oral_administration: Swallow whole with water, with or without food; avoid grapefruit. Do not replace a missed/vomited dose.
